newsitem.title: USA: Brooke's LeBow might reveal tobacco papers - ABC.
newsitem.headline: Brooke's LeBow might reveal tobacco papers - ABC.

text.p: Brooke Group Ltd Chairman Bennett LeBow is in negotiations to hand over evidence to some of the 18 attorneys general suing the tobacco industry, ABC news reported Wednesday.
The report said LeBow, whose company owns Liggett Group Inc, met with attorneys general "from several states in secret negotiations in various places around the country."
LeBow is offering 30 years' worth of documents from the industry's own research groups that show tobacco companies long knew that smoking was dangerous, ABC said.
"Sources who have seen the documents say they deal with tobacco companies' knowledge of the dangers of smoking and with their own cancelled efforts to create safer cigarettes," the report said.
In return for the evidence, LeBow is seeking immunity from all government lawsuits for Liggett, it said.
LeBow broke the code of the industry last year when he allowed Liggett to become the first cigarette company to settle a smoking-related lawsuit. No tobacco company had ever lost such a suit.
Neither LeBow nor his spokesman were immediately available for comment on the report.
